purpose: Increase ICLR-level experimental breadth without broadening the frozen STRI scientific claim scope, using first-party released artifacts, stronger practical baselines, heldout transfer, retrieval-budget interventions, and an independently labeled external relevance analogue.

baseline_paper_design_reference.paper: Skill Availability and Presentation Granularity in Large-Language-Model Agents: A Controlled SkillsBench Study
baseline_paper_design_reference.lesson_used: multi-domain controlled conditions and explicit skill-presentation interventions

baseline_paper_design_reference.paper: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work—Until They Don't
baseline_paper_design_reference.lesson_used: representation, retrieval, cross-framework, and failure-boundary controls rather than one aggregate result

baseline_paper_design_reference.paper: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
baseline_paper_design_reference.lesson_used: multiple agent environments and retrieval/evolution controls

baseline_paper_design_reference.paper: SkillRouter: Retrieve-and-Rerank Skill Selection for LLM Agents at Scale
baseline_paper_design_reference.lesson_used: expert task-skill relevance graph, single-versus-multi-skill stratification, top-K/reranking controls

practical_package_weight_baselines.interpretation: Released uniform package routing already attains the exact Level-1 worst-case optimum. Average-fit or inverse-coverage heuristics can improve a different objective or intuitive balancing criterion while substantially worsening worst-case representation distortion; the Level-1 residual is not a scalar-tuning failure.

skillrl_retrieval_budget_baselines.interpretation: The released SkillRL identity phenotype is specifically a provenance-priority by finite-budget interaction.

skillrouter_external_relevance_analogue.role: external retrieval-relevance analogue; NOT executable semantic support
skillrouter_external_relevance_analogue.interpretation: An independent expert relevance graph provides a strong equalizable negative analogue even when naive package-uniform exposure is highly nonuniform.

skillsbench_support_qualification.reason: Task-local availability is not independent complete semantic support. Absent local skills cannot be labeled unsupported without a separate support contract, so no SkillsBench R* certificate is reported.

manuscript_integration.quantitative_baseline_table: Table 2 now compares seven package-weight controllers plus semantic-first upper bound across L1 full, no-refit heldout, Level-3, and logical regimes.
manuscript_integration.external_boundary_table: Table 3 adds the SkillRouter core relevance analogue with an explicit relevance-not-support footnote.
manuscript_integration.figure_3: Two-panel boundary figure: support/relevance geometry on the left and SkillRL retrieval-budget sweep with capacity recovery on the right.
manuscript_integration.skillsbench_fail_closed: Experimental Setup explicitly records the 79/87 support-qualification mismatch and reports no R* from SkillsBench.
